source.title: Analysis and Evaluation of Synthetic Data Generation in Speech Dysfluency Detection
source.authors: Jinming Zhang; Xuanru Zhou; Jia-Chen Lian; Shuhe Li; William Li; Z. Ezzes; R. Bogley; L. Wauters; Z. Miller; J. Vonk; Brittany T. Morin; M. Gorno-Tempini; G. Anumanchipalli

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures downstream dysfluency-detection performance while varying training-data size. This bears on downstream performance scaling, but it does not measure language-model pretraining loss or parameter/compute scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. but does not test their language-model loss laws. Its own relevant result is a speech dysfluency-detection data-size experiment reporting F1 scores on SEP-28k. Other speech, dataset-quality, and detection results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The 'scaling law' experiment (Sec. 4.3.3, Fig. 5, Table 3) varies fine-tuning data size for a Whisper dysfluency detector and reports F1. It does not test any version. V6 concerns downstream gains from model or pretraining scale, or from pretraining loss, and this is fine-tuning data size. V5 concerns the power-law form, but no loss is reported, no curve is fitted, and bounded F1 near ceiling cannot show a power law. The text cites Kaplan et al. only to frame the experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: F1 reaches a substantial level at 3×4000 samples, gains marginally at 3×12000, then plateaus or slightly declines. The authors read this as an optimal dataset-size threshold for efficient training.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies synthetic training-data size for a speech dysfluency detector and evaluates F1. It does not use language-model held-out cross-entropy or sweep parameter count, tokens, or training compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-data size changes the reported F1 scores; the paper reports marginal gains followed by a plateau or slight decline, with category-specific changes in Table 3.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning Whisper-large-v3-turbo on synthetic dysfluency data: F1 on SEP-28k changes mixed from 3×4000 to 3×12000 samples per type, rising in four categories and falling in two. Authors report marginal gains, then a plateau or slight decline with more data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream task performance of a fine-tuned speech model saturates with fine-tuning data size rather than following a power law.

record.problems: The relevant scaling result uses one speech-detection setup and reports no uncertainty estimates. The text gives no aggregate F1 values for the broader scaling curve; Figure 5 is the only displayed curve for that analysis.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss curve or power-law fit in speech or fine-tuning; only F1 at a few data sizes.
No variation of model or pretraining scale; no pretraining loss as a predictor.
No fitted exponents or comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V6 labels are removed because the rows measure fine-tuning data size, not model or pretraining scale. Table 4 (TER/TD) also compares the two data sizes, but it is likewise outside every version. No uncertainty is reported, and Fig. 5 values are unreadable in the extracted text.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or scaling over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small language-model runs to larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or compute sweep.
No comparison of architecture depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies speech dysfluency detection, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds for loss in another modality or training regime.
Tests downstream F1 against synthetic training-data size in one speech-detection setup; does not test pretraining loss as a predictor, language-model scale, or other downstream tasks.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or comparison of fitting choices. It reports a plateau or slight decline in downstream F1 with more data, not curvature in language-model loss.

conditions.value: 3×4000 samples compared with 3×12000 samples and further expansion

rows.measure: F1 scores; aggregate details not stated
rows.baseline: The model reaches a substantial performance level at 3×4000 samples.
rows.value: Expansion to 3×12000 gives only marginal improvement; performance then plateaus or slightly declines.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend in text but gives no aggregate F1 values for this scaling result.
rows.check: Text-only description of the Fig. 5 trend (marginal gain, then plateau or slight decline); no values, no loss, no fitted form.
